local.summary: Both CLIs anchor global rules on a shared import: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.codex/AGENTS.md each contain only an @-import of the common /Users/ichanhui/.agent-rules.md (Codex adds a context7 section and an @-import of ~/.codex/RTK.md). Codex centralizes nearly everything in ~/.codex/config.toml (TOML): model/reasoning/sandbox/approval prefs, [mcp_servers.*] tables, per-project trust_level, plugin enables, [hooks.state] trust hashes, and desktop/TUI prefs; hooks themselves live in ~/.codex/hooks.json using the exact same JSON schema as Claude Code hooks. Claude Code splits config across ~/.claude/settings.json (permissions, model, hooks, env, enabledPlugins, effortLevel), settings.local.json (allowlist + one hook), and ~/.claude.json whose only migratable pieces are the top-level mcpServers object and per-project projects["path"].mcpServers/allowedTools — the other ~80 top-level keys are app state/caches. Neither tool has a prompts/ or commands/ directory; reusable behavior lives as skills/<name>/SKILL.md in both, agents as *.toml (Codex) vs *.md+YAML-frontmatter (Claude). Two plaintext secrets were found (redacted): a CONTEXT7_API_KEY in ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.context7.http_headers] and a NOTION_API_KEY in ~/.claude/mcp.json — a migration tool must treat MCP env/header values as secret-bearing.

facts.detail: ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (1558 B, mode 600) is the global instructions file. It @-imports /Users/ichanhui/.agent-rules.md (shared with Claude Code) and /Users/ichanhui/.codex/RTK.md, plus an inline Codex-only context7 usage section. Import syntax: bare '@/absolute/path' on its own line. Backups AGENTS.md.bak-* sit alongside.

MCP servers live in ~/.codex/config.toml as TOML tables [mcp_servers.<name>]. Stdio servers use command/args/env keys (e.g. playwright: command="npx", args=["@playwright/mcp@latest"]; node_repl with [mcp_servers.node_repl.env] table and startup_timeout_sec). HTTP servers use url (+ type="http" for context7, plus [mcp_servers.context7.http_headers] which holds a plaintext CONTEXT7_API_KEY — REDACTED). enabled=false disables a server (figma-desktop, kakao, computer-use). Per-tool gating via [mcp_servers.<name>.tools.<tool>] approval_mode="approve".

Top of config.toml: personality="pragmatic", model="gpt-5.6-sol", model_reasoning_effort="medium", plan_mode_reasoning_effort="high", sandbox_mode="danger-full-access", approval_policy="never", approvals_reviewer="user", service_tier="default", notify=[<app path>, "turn-ended"]. Also [features] (memories=true, js_repl=false), [memories] (generate/use), [tui] status_line array, [notice], and [desktop] GUI prefs including git-commit-instructions and git-pr-instructions multiline strings (Korean Conventional-Commits policy) — all migratable preference material.

config.toml holds ~45 [projects."<abs path>"] tables each with trust_level="trusted" (Codex's analog of Claude's per-project trust dialog), plus [shell_environment_policy] inherit="core" and a [shell_environment_policy.set] table injecting env vars (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 etc.) — maps to Claude settings.json env key.

~/.codex/hooks.json uses the SAME JSON schema as Claude Code hooks: {"hooks": {"PreToolUse": [{matcher, hooks:[{type:"command", command, timeout}]}], ...}} with events PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, SessionStart, Stop, Notification. It even reuses Claude-side scripts: python3 ~/.claude/hooks/env-file-guard.py --codex and ~/.claude/scripts/cleanup-playwright-mcp.sh. Hook helper scripts live in ~/.codex/hooks/ (codex-notify.sh, context-mode-cache-heal.mjs, gsd-*.js/sh). config.toml [hooks.state] records sha256 trusted_hash per hook entry (path:event:index:index keys) — a trust cache a migration tool must regenerate, not copy.

~/.codex/rules/default.rules is a line-oriented DSL: prefix_rule(pattern=["git", "add", ...], decision="allow") — argv-prefix command allowlist, Codex's analog of Claude's permissions.allow Bash() patterns. ~50 accumulated rules.

No ~/.codex/prompts/ directory exists. Reusable behavior: ~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (3 skills: codex-token-efficient-orchestrator, pdf, playwright — same Agent Skills layout as Claude). Subagents: ~/.codex/agents/*.toml (33 gsd-* files), TOML format with description and developer_instructions='''...''' keys (vs Claude's Markdown+frontmatter). ~/.codex/keybindings.json is a JSON array of {command, key} (one binding: realtimeVoice/Alt+V). Plugin enables are in config.toml [plugins."name@marketplace"] enabled=true/false with [marketplaces.*] source definitions.

auth.json (4134 B, mode 600) — NOT read per safety rule; holds credentials. Non-migratable state: .codex-global-state.json (~1 MB), history.jsonl, session_index.jsonl, sessions/, archived_sessions/, logs_2.sqlite (2.1 GB), state_5.sqlite, memories_1.sqlite, goals_1.sqlite, queue_1.sqlite, memories/ (MEMORY.md, raw_memories.md — user memory feature, arguably exportable), shell_snapshots/, worktrees/, generated_images/.

~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (169 B) contains only a pointer that @-imports /Users/ichanhui/.agent-rules.md — the same shared rules file Codex's AGENTS.md imports. The real rule content (interaction style, planning, security, git policy, etc.) lives in ~/.agent-rules.md, which is the single source of truth for both tools by design.

~/.claude/settings.json keys: env (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1), permissions {allow: [Read(//Users/ichanhui/Documents/**)], deny: 26 Read/Edit patterns blocking .env*/ssh keys/credentials, defaultMode: "auto"}, model: "claude-fable-5[1m]", hooks (SessionStart x3, WorktreeCreate, PreToolUse env-file-guard.py), enabledPlugins (4 name@marketplace booleans), extraKnownMarketplaces (github repo sources), effortLevel: "xhigh", tui: "fullscreen", skipAutoPermissionPrompt: true. settings.local.json adds permissions.allow (~38 Bash/MCP/Skill entries) and a PostToolUse hook (impeccable design detector). Multiple settings.json.bak-* backups alongside.

Three surfaces. (1) ~/.claude.json top-level "mcpServers" key — user-scope servers as JSON objects: context7, playwright, node_repl, codex-computer-use (type:"stdio" with command/args/env) and figma-desktop (type:"http" with url). (2) ~/.claude.json projects["<path>"].mcpServers — project-scope; exactly one project (StartUm_WEB) defines "notion". Project entries also carry enabledMcpjsonServers/disabledMcpjsonServers and allowedTools. (3) ~/.claude/mcp.json — standalone {"mcpServers": {...}} JSON (context7, github via ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN} env ref, Figma Desktop url, Notion with a PLAINTEXT NOTION_API_KEY — REDACTED, Playwright); note this is not a standard Claude Code auto-load path, likely legacy/hand-made.

~80 top-level keys; nearly all are app state/caches (numStartups, tipsHistory, cachedStatsigGates, oauthAccount, machineID, toolUsage, skillUsage, feedbackSurveyState, model/cost caches, onboarding+migration flags, etc.). Migratable keys: mcpServers (dict) and projects (dict of 49 per-path entries whose migratable fields are allowedTools, mcpServers, enabledMcpjsonServers, disabledMcpjsonServers, hasTrustDialogAccepted; the rest are per-project session stats). File is mode 600, 100 KB.

No ~/.claude/commands/ and no ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Skills: ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (~127 dirs: gsd-*, gstack suite, impeccable, commit-grouping, etc.) — same format as Codex skills. Agents: ~/.claude/agents/*.md (33 gsd-* files), Markdown with YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, color) — parallel set to Codex's *.toml agents with identical names/descriptions. Hook scripts: ~/.claude/hooks/ (env-file-guard.py + test, context-mode-cache-heal.mjs, gsd-*.js/sh — mirrors ~/.codex/hooks/) and ~/.claude/scripts/ (cleanup-playwright-mcp.sh, link-worktree-claude-state.sh) shared by both tools' hook configs. Plugin state: ~/.claude/plugins/ (installed_plugins.json, known_marketplaces.json, blocklist.json, cache/, data/, marketplaces/ — contents skipped per task).

Direct mappings: [mcp_servers.<name>] TOML tables <-> mcpServers JSON objects (command/args/env and url fields are near-identical; Codex adds enabled, startup_timeout_sec, http_headers, per-tool approval_mode). hooks.json schema is byte-compatible with Claude settings hooks (both tools already share the same scripts and even the same GSD hook set duplicated in both hooks/ dirs). Rules: shared ~/.agent-rules.md via @import in both entry files. Permissions: Claude permissions.allow/deny glob patterns vs Codex prefix_rule argv patterns + approval_policy/sandbox_mode — semantic translation needed, not syntactic. Agents: same content, TOML (developer_instructions) vs MD (frontmatter) — format conversion needed. Codex-only surfaces with no Claude analog: [projects.*] trust_level, [desktop] git-commit/pr-instructions, [shell_environment_policy], keybindings.json, rules DSL.

gaps: ~/.codex/auth.json (4134 B, mode 600) not read per safety rules — credential storage format unverified.

Whether ~/.claude/mcp.json is actually loaded by current Claude Code versions could not be verified locally; it is not a documented auto-load path (documented scopes are ~/.claude.json user scope and project .mcp.json), so it may be dead legacy config — but it still contains a live-looking Notion API key that a migration tool must not copy verbatim.
~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json (~1 MB) and the sqlite databases were not parsed — treated as non-migratable app state without inspection.

~/.claude/plugins/ and ~/.codex/plugins/cache contents skipped per task instructions; installed-plugin manifests (installed_plugins.json, known_marketplaces.json) were listed but not diffed against Codex's [plugins.*]/[marketplaces.*] tables.

Two plaintext secrets exist in readable config (CONTEXT7_API_KEY in ~/.codex/config.toml http_headers; NOTION_API_KEY in ~/.claude/mcp.json) — values were seen during required reads but are redacted from this report; flagging so the migration tool design includes a secret-redaction pass.
~/.codex/memories/ (MEMORY.md, raw_memories.md) contents not read — existence noted; whether user wants memories migrated is a product decision, not verified.

codex.summary: As of August 2026, Codex CLI's config surface centers on $CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex): config.toml (user), .codex/config.toml (project, trusted only), profile files (~/.codex/<name>.config.toml — the old [profiles.x] table in config.toml is deprecated since 0.134.0), and admin layers /etc/codex/managed_config.toml + /etc/codex/requirements.toml. Official docs moved: developers.openai.com/codex/* now 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*, and the github.com/openai/codex/docs/*.md files are stubs pointing there. Key keys: model, model_provider(+[model_providers.*]), approval_policy (untrusted/on-request/never), sandbox_mode (read-only/workspace-write/danger-full-access) with [sandbox_workspace_write], [mcp_servers.*] (stdio: command/args/env; HTTP: url/bearer_token_env_var), notify = ["prog","arg"], [projects."/abs/path"] trust_level = "trusted", [features] flags, and [[hooks.EventName]] tables. Hooks are fully supported (hooks.json or [hooks] in config.toml; events PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, Pre/PostCompact, Stop, SubagentStart/Stop, SessionStart/End; stdin JSON in, stdout JSON out, exit 2 = block). AGENTS.md discovery: ~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md else ~/.codex/AGENTS.md globally, then per-directory from git root down to cwd (AGENTS.override.md > AGENTS.md > project_doc_fallback_filenames, one file per dir), capped at project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default). Custom prompts (~/.codex/prompts/*.md, /prompts:name, $1-$9/$ARGUMENTS/$KEY) are deprecated in favor of skills (~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md). Auth lives in ~/.codex/auth.json (or OS keyring via cli_auth_credentials_store); other setup state includes sessions/rollouts (~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl), history.jsonl, log/, and .codexignore in repos.

facts.detail: github.com/openai/codex/docs/*.md (config.md, agents_md.md, authentication.md) are now stubs linking to developers.openai.com/codex/*, which 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*. A migration tool should treat learn.chatgpt.com as the canonical doc host but developers.openai.com URLs still resolve.

User config: ~/.codex/config.toml (CODEX_HOME env var overrides the ~/.codex base dir). Project overrides: .codex/config.toml inside a trusted project (walked from project root down to cwd; closest wins). Precedence high→low: CLI flags / -c key=value overrides > project .codex/config.toml > profile file ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml > user ~/.codex/config.toml > system /etc/codex/config.toml > built-in defaults. --strict-config makes unrecognized keys an error; /debug-config shows layers in precedence order.

model = "gpt-5.5" ; model_provider = "openai" ; model_context_window = 128000 ; model_auto_compact_token_limit ; model_reasoning_effort = "minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh" ; model_reasoning_summary = "auto|concise|detailed|none" ; model_verbosity = "low|medium|high".

[model_providers.<id>] with keys: name, base_url, env_key (env var holding the API key), env_http_headers = { "X-Header" = "ENV_NAME" }, http_headers, query_params, request_max_retries, stream_idle_timeout_ms, stream_max_retries, wire_api = "responses" (or "chat"), plus optional [model_providers.<id>.auth] with command/args/cwd/timeout_ms/refresh_interval_ms for token-fetching commands. Example: [model_providers.custom]
name = "Custom Provider"
base_url = "https://custom-api.example.com"
env_key = "CUSTOM_API_KEY".

approval_policy = "untrusted" | "on-request" | "never". Also a granular form: [approval_policy.granular] with sandbox_approval, rules, mcp_elicitations, request_permissions, skill_approval booleans; and approvals_reviewer = "user" | "auto_review".

sandbox_mode = "read-only" | "workspace-write" | "danger-full-access". Companion table: [sandbox_workspace_write] with network_access = true|false, writable_roots = ["/path"], exclude_slash_tmp, exclude_tmpdir_env_var. Newer granular system: [permissions.<profile>] tables with extends = ":read-only"|":workspace", [.filesystem] path→"read"/"write" glob maps, [.network] domain allow/deny rules; built-in profiles :read-only, :workspace, :danger-full-access. Windows: [windows] sandbox = "elevated".

[mcp_servers.<name>]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]
env_vars = ["LOCAL_TOKEN"]  # env vars forwarded from parent
[mcp_servers.<name>.env]
MY_ENV_VAR = "MY_ENV_VALUE"
Optional: cwd, enabled = true|false, required, startup_timeout_sec (default 10), tool_timeout_sec (default 60), enabled_tools/disabled_tools arrays, default_tools_approval_mode = "auto"|"prompt"|"writes"|"approve", per-tool [mcp_servers.<name>.tools.<tool>] approval_mode/enabled.

[mcp_servers.<name>]
url = "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "FIGMA_OAUTH_TOKEN"
http_headers = { "X-Figma-Region" = "us-east-1" }
Optional: env_http_headers, auth = "oauth" (default) | "chatgpt", scopes, oauth_resource, startup_timeout_sec. CLI management: codex mcp add <name> --env VAR=VALUE -- <command> ; codex mcp list ; codex mcp login <name>. MCP OAuth creds: mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "file"|"keyring"|"auto", mcp_oauth_callback_port/url.

Current form: one file per profile at ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml containing plain top-level keys (e.g. model = "gpt-5.5", model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh", approval_policy = "on-request"), activated with codex --profile <name>. The legacy inline form — profile = "o3" at top level plus [profiles.o3] tables inside config.toml — is documented as deprecated as of version 0.134.0, but a migration tool should still parse the legacy [profiles.<name>] tables found in older config.toml files.

notify = ["python3", "/path/to/notify.py"] — array of program + args. Codex appends a single JSON argument with fields like type, thread-id, input-messages, last-assistant-message. Separate TUI-only notifications live under [tui] notifications/notification_method ("auto"|"osc9"|"bel")/notification_condition ("unfocused"|"always").

[projects."/home/user/my-project"]\ntrust_level = "trusted"  # or "untrusted"\nStored in ~/.codex/config.toml; the path is a quoted absolute-path key. Trust gates whether the project's .codex/config.toml, .codex/hooks.json, and project skills layers are honored.

1) Global: in CODEX_HOME (~/.codex), Codex reads AGENTS.override.md if it exists, otherwise AGENTS.md. 2) Project: from the Git root down to the current directory, each directory is checked; within a directory the order is AGENTS.override.md, then AGENTS.md, then fallback names from project_doc_fallback_filenames (config key, e.g. ["AGENTS.md", "AI.md"] or TEAM_GUIDE.md/.agents.md), at most one file per directory. Files are concatenated root-down joined with blank lines; files closer to cwd effectively override because they appear later in the combined prompt. project_root_markers = [".git", ...] controls root detection.

project_doc_max_bytes in config.toml caps the combined instruction bytes: 32 KiB (32768) by default. Codex skips empty files and stops adding files once the combined size reaches the limit; raise it (e.g. project_doc_max_bytes = 65536) or split instructions across nested directories.

Markdown files in ~/.codex/prompts/ ($CODEX_HOME/prompts); only top-level .md files are scanned, subdirectories ignored. Optional YAML frontmatter: description and argument-hint. Invoked as slash commands: /prompts:<filename> (type / for the menu). Placeholders: $1–$9 positional (space-separated args), $ARGUMENTS = all args, $UPPERCASE_NAME named args supplied as KEY=value (quote values with spaces), $$ = literal $. Restart Codex/new chat after edits. Officially deprecated in favor of skills (which support implicit invocation and version-control sharing).

Yes, Codex supports lifecycle hooks. Config locations (precedence order): ~/.codex/hooks.json, ~/.codex/config.toml [hooks] tables, <repo>/.codex/hooks.json, <repo>/.codex/config.toml. Project hooks only run when the .codex layer is trusted. Feature-gated via [features] hooks = true (default true). Non-managed command hooks must be reviewed/trusted via /hooks (trust recorded against hook hash); --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust skips for one invocation. Admins can set allow_managed_hooks_only = true in requirements.toml.

Events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd. hooks.json shape: {"hooks": {"SessionStart": [{"matcher": "startup|resume", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "python3 ~/.codex/hooks/session_start.py", "statusMessage": "...", "additionalContextLimit": 5000}]}]}}. TOML equivalent: [[hooks.SessionStart]] matcher = "..." then [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]] type = "command", command = '...'. Matcher is regex ("*", "" or omitted = all; e.g. Bash, ^apply_patch$, Edit|Write). Contract: JSON on stdin (session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, model + event fields like tool_name/tool_input); JSON on stdout ({continue, stopReason, systemMessage, hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext}); exit 0 = ok, exit 2 = block/deny with reason on stderr. Options: async = true (background), timeout (default 600s, SessionEnd 1s), additionalContextLimit (default 2500), commandWindows.

Cached login credentials live at ~/.codex/auth.json by default ($CODEX_HOME/auth.json). cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" | "keyring" | "auto" (auto prefers OS keyring, falls back to file). API-key login: printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key. Enterprise pinning: forced_login_method = "chatgpt"|"api", forced_chatgpt_workspace_id = "<uuid>".

Full session transcripts ("rollouts") are JSONL files at ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-<uuid>.jsonl, used by codex resume; /rollout prints the current session's path. ~/.codex/history.jsonl stores one line per typed user turn ({session_id, ts, text}), governed by [history] persistence = "save-all" | "none" and max_bytes. Logs go to ~/.codex/log (configurable log_dir); sqlite_home sets the state DB dir.
facts.source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference (history keys) + session path corroborated by https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/06/05/codex-cli-session-lifecycle-archive-resume-fork-compact-management/ and https://betelgeuse.work/codex-resume/

facts.detail: .codexignore in the repo (gitignore syntax) keeps files out of the agent's file discovery/context; Codex also respects .gitignore. As of ~v0.135 the common file-discovery paths honor it, but it is context hygiene, not access control — shell commands (rg, cat) can still read ignored files; pair with permission-profile deny rules for real protection.

[features] table in config.toml: shell_tool, unified_exec, multi_agent, web_search, shell_snapshot, apps, remote_plugin, personality, fast_mode, goals, hooks, skill_mcp_dependency_install, enable_request_compression, prevent_idle_sleep, memories, plus nested [features.code_mode], [features.network_proxy], [features.rollout_budget]. Top-level web_search = "disabled|cached|indexed|live". suppress_unstable_features_warning = false.

Hard constraints: requirements.toml at /etc/codex/requirements.toml (Unix) or %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml (Windows), also deliverable as cloud policy via ChatGPT workspace login or MDM. Soft defaults: /etc/codex/managed_config.toml (skipped if absent). requirements.toml supports allow_managed_hooks_only = true to ignore user/project/session hook configs.

Personal skills: ~/.codex/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md ; project skills: .codex/skills/ at repo root. Same cross-agent SKILL.md format (frontmatter + instructions); optional Codex-specific openai.yaml alongside for UI hints/MCP dependencies. Repo doc: github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/docs/skills.md.

facts.topic: Other notable config keys for migration
facts.detail: file_opener = "vscode" (citation link handler); [shell_environment_policy] inherit = "all|core|none" with [.filters] include/exclude glob map and [.set] var map; [tui] theme/keymaps/status_line; developer_instructions and model_instructions_file; project_doc_fallback_filenames; check_for_update_on_startup; [otel] telemetry exporters; [agents] multi-agent config with per-agent config_file; [memories] table; oss_provider = "ollama" for codex --oss.

gaps: The exact ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl path pattern comes from reputable secondary sources (codex.danielvaughan.com, betelgeuse.work) — the official config reference documents [history] keys but the fetched pages did not state the sessions directory path verbatim.
Skills SKILL.md frontmatter field list and openai.yaml schema were not verified against the official skills doc page (repo docs/skills.md is a redirect stub; details came from secondary guides).
.codexignore semantics (which discovery paths honor it, version v0.135 claim) verified only via GitHub discussions/issues and secondary write-ups, not a dedicated official doc page.

The legacy [profiles.<name>] inline TOML shape (pre-0.134.0) is from historical knowledge of the repo docs; current docs only describe the new per-file profile format and note the deprecation — a migration tool should still handle both.

config-reference values were extracted by a summarizing fetch of learn.chatgpt.com; individual defaults (e.g. startup_timeout_sec = 10, additionalContextLimit = 2500) match the page as fetched but were not cross-checked against source code.
Exact per-event matcher value lists for hooks (which matcher strings each event supports) were referenced but not enumerated by the docs page fetched.

claude.summary: Claude Code's configuration surface spans user, project, and local scopes with distinct file locations and JSON/YAML formats for instructions, MCP servers, skills, settings, and plugins. User instructions live at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with @path imports; project instructions at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md. MCP servers are configured in ~/.claude.json (local/user scope), .mcp.json (project scope), or bundled in plugins. Skills use SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and live in ~/.claude/skills/ or .claude/skills/. Settings in settings.json control permissions (allow/deny/ask rules with glob patterns), hooks (event/matcher/command format), environment variables, and model configuration. Plugins package as directories with .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest. Skills can safely write their own supporting files but should use CLI commands (claude mcp add, /permissions) rather than directly editing configuration files.

facts.detail: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — personal instructions for all projects; loaded before project CLAUDE.md
./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md at project root; optional path-scoped rules in .claude/rules/*.md with 'paths:' frontmatter field
@path/to/file or @~/path syntax (relative to file location, not cwd); backtick-wrapping prevents import: `@README` reads as literal text; max 4 hops recursive
./CLAUDE.local.md — personal project-specific preferences; add to .gitignore (shares auto memory location per project git repo)
~/.claude.json under projects['/path/to/project'].mcpServers with JSON shape: {'type':'http|sse|ws|stdio','url':'...','command':'...','args':[...], 'env':{...}, 'headers':{...}, 'timeout': ms}
.mcp.json at project root with top-level 'mcpServers' object; same JSON structure as local scope; checked into version control
~/.claude.json with top-level 'mcpServers' (not nested under projects); applies across all projects on the machine
command (string, required), args (string array, optional), env (object with KEY=VALUE strings, optional), alwaysLoad (bool), timeout (ms integer)
type ('http', 'sse', or 'streamable-http'), url (string), headers (object), headersHelper (command string), timeout (ms), alwaysLoad (bool)

facts.topic: Programmatic Safety: Skills Writing Own Files
facts.detail: Safe: SKILL.md can reference ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} in allowed-tools rules; skills can write to their own directory and subdirectories without issue
Do NOT write ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json directly; use CLI commands: 'claude mcp add' for new servers, 'claude mcp remove' for deletion; JSON corruption risks prompt rejection
Do NOT edit settings.json permissions programmatically; use '/permissions' command in session or 'claude --allowedTools' at startup; auto-saves to .claude/settings.local.json with per-repo scope
Skills should NOT write to CLAUDE.md files; Claude loads them once at startup; use skills or hooks with /context to observe, not modify; team coordination needed for CLAUDE.md updates
Skills should NOT modify plugin.json or install plugins programmatically; use '/plugin install' command; plugins are validated at load time and cache-aware
Safe to write to settings.json 'env' block in some contexts (e.g., skill updating its own temporary vars), but changes require session reload; prefer passing via hook or skill invocation context
claude mcp add --transport [http|sse|ws|stdio] [--env KEY=VAL] [--header 'Auth: token'] [--scope local|project|user] <name> <url|command [args...]>; defaults to local scope
claude plugin validate ./plugin-dir [--strict] — checks plugin.json schema, skill structures, LSP configs, marketplace.json format; part of submission pipeline
~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with MEMORY.md (loaded up to 200 lines/25KB at session start) and topic .md files; auto memory disabled with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 or settings

prior.summary: 2026년 8월 기준 AI 코딩 에이전트 설정 이관/동기화의 선행 기술은 세 갈래다. (1) 허브-스포크 동기화 도구 — rulesync(9개 카테고리, 40+ 툴, import/convert 지원)와 ruler(31+ 툴, 일방향 배포 전용)가 성숙해 있고 둘 다 결정적(deterministic) 코드다. (2) 방향성 마이그레이션 도구 — Claude→Codex 방향은 OpenAI 공식 migrate-to-codex 스킬과 Codex CLI 네이티브 /import(v0.145+에서 Cursor·Claude Code의 설정·MCP·세션·커맨드까지 흡수)를 포함해 최소 6개(claude-to-codex, claude2codex, ccode-to-codex, cc2codex 등)로 포화 상태인 반면, 역방향 Codex→Claude는 stelabouras/Codex-to-Claude(config.toml 일부+세션만)와 MisterBrookT/codex2claude(세션 전용 플러그인) 정도로 희소하고, AGENTS.md→CLAUDE.md 변환·permissions/approval_policy 매핑·hooks 변환을 다루는 도구는 사실상 없다. (3) AGENTS.md 표준 — Linux Foundation 관리 하에 Codex·Cursor·Copilot·Gemini CLI 등 거의 모든 주요 툴이 네이티브 채택했으나 Claude Code만 2026년 8월 현재 미지원(CLAUDE.md에서 @AGENTS.md import 또는 symlink 우회만 가능). 차별화 공백은 명확하다 — "Codex→Claude 방향의 전체 설정(config.toml→settings.json, approval_policy→permissions, AGENTS.md→CLAUDE.md, hooks, prompts→commands) 마이그레이션"을 결정적으로 처리하는 도구는 존재하지 않으며, 기존 도구들은 의미 손실이 큰 항목(권한 모델 세분성 차이, hooks 이벤트 모델 차이, output style)을 전부 수동 검토로 미룬다.

facts.detail: Node.js/TypeScript 결정적 CLI. .rulesync/ 단일 소스에서 40+ 툴(Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI 등)로 생성. 지원 카테고리 9종: rules, mcp, commands, subagents, skills, hooks, permissions, ignore(deprecated), checks. Claude Code는 전 기능, Codex CLI는 ignore 제외 전 기능 매트릭스에 표시. 명령: init/generate/import/convert/fetch. import는 Cursor·Claude Code·Copilot 등 기존 설정 역수입, convert는 .rulesync/ 없이 툴 간 직접 변환. 미커버: 일부 기능은 툴별로 'simulated'(네이티브 미지원 툴에서 흉내), 세션/히스토리 이관 없음, 의미 변환(권한 모델 차이 등)은 하지 않음.

npm @intellectronica/ruler, TypeScript 결정적 CLI. .ruler/ 디렉토리의 Markdown rules + ruler.toml의 MCP 서버 설정 + skills + subagents(실험적) + .gitignore 관리 블록을 31+ 에이전트(Copilot, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI 등)에 일방향 배포. 명령: ruler init / ruler apply (--agents, --nested, --dry-run, --no-mcp 등). 미커버: import 없음(일방향 전용), commands/hooks/permissions/settings 미지원, skills는 네이티브 지원 없는 에이전트 스킵, subagents revert 명령 없음, 홈 디렉토리 쓰기 금지.

Linux Foundation 산하 Agentic AI Foundation이 관리(2025-12 기증)하는 오픈 포맷. 60,000+ 저장소 채택. OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Jules, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Zed, Warp, Devin, Factory, Junie 등 27+ 툴이 네이티브 읽기 지원. 필수 필드 없는 자유 Markdown.

2026년 8월(Claude Code 2.1.201, 2026-07 기준) 현재 Claude Code는 AGENTS.md를 네이티브로 읽지 않고 CLAUDE.md만 읽는 유일한 주요 홀드아웃. anthropics/claude-code#34235 등 기능 요청은 오픈 상태로 로드맵 신호 없음. 공식 우회는 CLAUDE.md 안에 '@AGENTS.md' import 한 줄을 두거나 'ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md' symlink. agents.md 사이트에 Claude Code가 목록에 있으나 이는 우회 기반.

facts.topic: Codex CLI 네이티브 /import (공식, 최대 경쟁 선행 기술)
facts.detail: Codex CLI v0.128~0.130에서 에이전트 마이그레이션 시스템 도입, v0.145(2026-07-21)에서 /import가 Cursor·Claude Code의 settings, MCP 서버, plugins, sessions, commands, 프로젝트 memories까지 확장, v0.147은 Cursor 관리 skills도 수입. 결정적·규칙 기반, --scan-only/--plan/--doctor/--dry-run 지원. 한계: 단방향(역동기화 없음), Claude hooks의 조건 그룹·async 핸들러 제외, $ARGUMENTS·@file 런타임 확장 정적 변환 불가. 반대 방향(Claude Code가 Codex를 import)은 공식 기능이 존재하지 않음.

OpenAI 공식 skills 저장소의 마이그레이션 스킬. CLAUDE.md→AGENTS.md 병합, settings.json→config.toml, slash commands→.agents/skills/, MCP→[mcp_servers.*], subagents→.codex/agents/*.toml, 최근 30일 세션까지 8개 카테고리 이관. Claude Code 소스가 가장 성숙, Cursor/Aider/Gemini CLI는 지원 편차.

npx claude-to-codex@latest, 기본 dry-run. CLAUDE.md→AGENTS.md, .claude/skills/→.agents/skills/, .claude/commands/→skills 변환, .claude/agents/→.codex/config.toml+.codex/agents/*.toml, 경로 참조 재작성. 결정적 코드. 명시적 미커버: maxTurns, preloaded skills, hooks, memory, background, isolation(Codex 대응물 없어 드롭). Claude→Codex 단방향.

npx claude2codex init/migrate. plugins, MCP, memory 파일, config.toml, hooks.json, AGENTS.md, skills/agents 트리 이관. 자동 스냅샷+실패 시 롤백, 비파괴 머지, 멱등 재실행. 제작자 주장 약 95% 자동 변환, 나머지는 conflict report로 수동 처리. Claude→Codex 단방향, 결정적.

Claude skills/agents→Codex 네이티브 skill 패키지·custom-agent TOML로 의미 보존 매핑. 마이그레이션 위험을 MECHANICAL/MANUAL/REFACTOR로 분류, 구조 검증·진행 추적. Python 스크립트 기반 결정적 변환(Codex CLI 안에서 실행하는 워크플로우). 실험적, Claude→Codex 단방향, commands/hooks/settings 범위 불명확.

Codex→Claude 방향의 몇 안 되는 도구. Python 3.11+ 결정적 스크립트. ~/.codex/config.toml→~/.claude/settings.json(MCP 서버, personality→customInstructions, 모델명은 제안만), ~/.codex/sessions/→~/.claude/projects/ JSONL 세션 변환. --dry-run/--inspect/--since/--limit 지원. 미커버: AGENTS.md→CLAUDE.md 변환 없음, prompts/commands 없음, profiles 없음, approval_policy→permissions 매핑 없음, hooks 없음.

Codex 세션을 Claude Code로 수입해 claude --resume으로 이어가는 원커맨드 Claude Code 플러그인(/plugin marketplace add 방식). transession(Rust) 범용 IR로 JSONL 상호 변환, 중복 방지 원장 유지. 세션 전용 — 설정·rules·MCP·commands·permissions는 전혀 다루지 않음. reasoning payload와 런타임 캐시는 드롭.
Codex CLI와 Claude Code 간 JSONL 세션을 양방향 변환해 이어서 재개하는 브리지. 세션 전용, 설정 카테고리 미커버.

커뮤니티 마이그레이션 가이드(12개 설정 표면 매핑)가 지적하는 비결정적 갭 3가지: (1) 권한 모델 — Claude의 per-command glob allowlist vs Codex의 approval_policy+sandbox_mode 조립식 티어는 세분성이 달라 손실 변환, (2) hooks 이벤트 모델 차이 — ConfigChange 등 대응 이벤트 부재, (3) outputStyle — Codex에 대응물 없음. 역방향(Codex→Claude)에서도 동일한 의미 매핑 문제가 미해결 영역.

mcpmarket.com에 'Claude Code Migrator'(Cursor/Copilot/Aider 등의 설정 파일을 스캔·정리해 Claude Code로 이관)와 'Migration Guides' 스킬이 등재 — AI 구동 Claude 스킬 형태로 추정되나 페이지가 429로 상세 검증 불가. Codex CLI를 소스로 명시한 into-Claude 스킬은 검색상 확인되지 않음.

GitHub 'codex to claude' 검색 결과 대부분은 설정 이관이 아니라 API 프록시(Codex 구독을 Claude Code에서 쓰기: shuiyu486/CodexToClaude, archibate/codex-to-claude 등)이거나 세션 전용 도구. 'Codex→Claude 전체 설정 마이그레이션'(config.toml→settings.json 전반, AGENTS.md→CLAUDE.md, prompts→commands, MCP TOML→.mcp.json, approval_policy→permissions 의미 매핑, hooks 변환, 충돌 리포트)을 다루는 전용 도구는 2026-08 현재 부재. rulesync convert가 이론상 가장 근접하지만 허브 포맷 경유의 범용 변환이라 Codex 특화 의미 매핑·세션·설정 병합 전략이 없음.

gaps: mcpmarket.com의 'Claude Code Migrator'·'Migration Guides' 스킬 상세(제작자, AI 구동 여부, Codex 소스 지원 여부) — 페이지가 HTTP 429로 두 차례 차단되어 검색 스니펫 수준만 확인
rulesync import가 지원하는 정확한 소스 툴 전체 목록 — README는 Cursor/Claude Code/Copilot 예시만 명시, Codex CLI import 가능 여부는 매트릭스에서 직접 확인 못 함
Codex CLI /import의 정확한 도입 버전(0.128~0.130, 0.140, 0.145, 0.147 등) — 서드파티 블로그(codex.danielvaughan.com) 기반이며 OpenAI 공식 changelog로 교차 검증하지 않음
검색 결과에 언급된 'cc-migrate' npm 패키지 — 독립 소스로 실존 검증하지 못함(검색 요약에만 등장)
yibie/plugin-claude-2-codex, ussumant/cc2codex의 상세 커버리지 — 존재만 확인, README 미조사
Gemini CLI·Copilot의 자체 import/마이그레이션 기능 존재 여부 — AGENTS.md 네이티브 읽기 외 별도 조사하지 않음
